title: Surjectivity of a representable morphism of algebraic spaces is surjectivity on the underlying topological spaces

difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: a representable morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S is surjective in the representable sense if and only if |f| : |X| -> |Y| is surjective (source lines 817-823). The proof unwinds the definition: representable surjectivity means that every base change f_T : T x_Y X -> T along a morphism from a scheme is a surjective morphism of schemes, which is equivalent to |f_T| being surjective; the comparison map |T x_Y X| -> |T| x_{|Y|} |X| is always surjective, so surjectivity of |f| propagates to every |f_T|, and conversely taking T to be the spectrum of a field recovers surjectivity of |f|.
